family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Start with the basal aquatic leaf rosette and the emergent inflorescence. In the local Sagittaria anchor, confirm 3-part flowers, female flowers below male flowers, and a head of many achenes.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Aquatic or marsh herbs, often rhizomatous/corm-forming, with strong heterophylly between submerged and emergent leaves.
family_diagnostics.flowers: Typically 3 sepals + 3 petals; numerous stamens and/or carpels are common in family members.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Often aggregates of achenes; local Sagittaria makes rough spherical heads of many beaked achenes.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: LOOK HERE FIRST: Inspect a single flower and a ripe fruit, not leaf outline. Sagittaria has separate staminate and pistillate flowers, commonly female below male on the axis; Echinodorus has bisexual flowers with stamens and many free carpels together. Both can make round heads of achenes. Alismataceae free superior carpels contrast with the fused inferior ovary of Hydrocharitaceae.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: whole plant → high-value structure → reproductive confirmation → tie-breaker
visual_lesson.intro: The best local lesson is that one aquatic species can look radically different above and below water—and the reproductive stalk ties those forms together.

steps.title: 1 · Notice heterophylly
steps.look_for: Narrow submerged phyllodes versus broader emergent blades on the same species.
steps.why_it_matters: Aquatic plants can change leaf form dramatically with water depth.

steps.title: 2 · Read the flower stalk vertically
steps.look_for: Pistillate flowers lower on the raceme and staminate flowers above.
steps.why_it_matters: Inflorescence position is a high-value Sagittaria teaching character.

steps.title: 3 · Count in threes
steps.look_for: Three white petals and the 3-part monocot flower plan.
steps.why_it_matters: Connects the aquatic gestalt to reproductive structure.

steps.title: 4 · Follow female flower to achene head
steps.look_for: A rough spherical head composed of many small beaked achenes.
steps.why_it_matters: The aggregate fruit confirms the reproductive pattern.

comparisons.title: Sagittaria platyphylla vs arrow-leaved Sagittaria
comparisons.rule: Do not require deep arrow-shaped basal lobes; S. platyphylla often has ovate to linear-ovate emergent blades and narrow submerged leaves.

visual_lesson.caveat: The current lesson is structurally complete, but public/reusable diagnostic photo files are still a visual-polish task.
